fullName: UP Police Constable — Direct Recruitment of Constable (Civil Police) and equivalent posts, Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board (UPPRPB)
overview: UP Police Constable is the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board's biggest recruitment drive. One notification fills **Constable (Civil Police), Armed Police, Special Security Force, Mounted Police, Mahila Battalion and Jail Warder** posts, all at **Pay Matrix Level 3 (₹21,700–69,100)**. The selection runs on a simple spine: an **offline OMR written exam (150 questions, 300 marks, 2 hours)**, then document verification with the physical standard test, a **qualifying running race (PET)**, and a final merit list built purely from **written exam marks** — there is no interview. The paper has four subjects: **General Knowledge (with heavy Uttar Pradesh content), General Hindi, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Mental Aptitude, IQ and Reasoning**. There is no English paper; Hindi grammar and vocabulary are tested in Hindi. Because lakhs of candidates sit in many shifts, scores are **normalised across shifts**, so your rank depends on the adjusted score, not the raw one. The PET is a pass-or-fail run, but the written exam is where the merit list is actually made, so speed and accuracy on the OMR sheet decide selection.

latestCycle.status: **Written exam was held on 8, 9 and 10 June 2026** (two shifts a day) for the direct recruitment notified on 31 December 2025 (Advertisement 07/2025) with **32,679 vacancies**. The **written result was declared on 31 July 2026** and around **76,184 candidates were shortlisted for document verification/PST and PET** (figure from dated news reports — cross-check the shortlist notice on uppbpb.gov.in). The **PET is being held from 1 to 7 October 2026**, with a **reserve day of 8 October 2026** for Moradabad, Meerut and Ghaziabad centres, per the board's PET notice dated 24 September 2026; centre-wise date-change notices (for example Gorakhpur and Azamgarh, 5 October 2026) are published on uppbpb.gov.in. After the PET, the board moves to DV completion and the final merit list.

Age is counted as on **1 July 2025**. Applications went through **One Time Registration (OTR)** on the board's portal. About **28.86 lakh candidates** had applied for the June 2026 exam and about **21.9 lakh appeared** (roughly 75.9 per cent attendance — dated news reports; the board's own figures may differ). Vertical and horizontal reservations apply **only to Uttar Pradesh natives**.

statusPhases.status: **Written result is out** (declared 31 July 2026) with a category-wise and gender-wise cutoff, and candidates were called for document verification/PST and PET. If you are shortlisted, keep every original certificate ready — caste, domicile, Class 10 and 12 marksheets — in the formats the notice prescribes.

**PET schedule and admit cards announced.** The board's PET notice dated 24 September 2026 fixed the PET for **1–7 October 2026**, with a reserve day of **8 October 2026** for Moradabad, Meerut and Ghaziabad centres, and put the admit-card download link on uppbpb.gov.in. Male candidates run 4.8 km in 25 minutes, female candidates 2.4 km in 14 minutes; failing the race ends the candidature.

**PET is under way** from 1 October 2026. Centre-wise instructions and date-change notices (for example Gorakhpur and Azamgarh, 5 October 2026) are published on uppbpb.gov.in — check your own centre's notice before travelling.

**Next: DV completion and final merit list.** The board has not announced a date for the final selection list — watch uppbpb.gov.in. The merit list is drawn from written exam marks, category-wise, after the PET and medical stages.

stages.notes: The official advertisement fixes the total — **150 questions, 2 marks each, 300 marks, 2 hours, four subjects, OMR mode** — and gives the full subject-wise syllabus, but does not print a per-subject question count. The **38/37/38/37 split shown here is the pattern of the previous (2024) cycle's paper**, reproduced in dated exam reports; confirm the final split from the board's exam-day notice. **No sectional timing.** Minimum qualifying marks in the written exam: **30% for Unreserved, 25% for OBC, 20% for SC/ST**. Scores are normalised across shifts using the board's published procedure.

stages.name: Document verification and Physical Standard Test (PST)
stages.nature: Qualifying — candidates shortlisted from the written result in a multiple of the vacancies
stages.notes: Original documents are checked (education, age, caste in the prescribed Prakoshtha formats, UP residence certificate for reservation, DigiLocker uploads). Physical standards per the advertisement: **male minimum height 168 cm (160 cm for ST), chest 79 cm unexpanded and 84 cm expanded with a minimum 5 cm expansion; female minimum height 152 cm (147 cm for ST), minimum weight 40 kg**. Height and chest measured earlier in other recruitments do not count; the measurement at this stage is final.

stages.name: Physical Efficiency Test (PET) — qualifying race
stages.nature: Qualifying (pass or fail); failing candidates are eliminated at this level
stages.notes: Only candidates who clear document verification and the physical standard test appear in the PET. **Male candidates must complete a 4.8 km run within 25 minutes; female candidates must complete a 2.4 km run within 14 minutes.** Candidates who do not finish within the time do not qualify and are removed at the same level. There is no second chance after the notified last date.

eligibility.nationality: Citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal or Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1 January 1962 for permanent settlement, or a person of Indian origin migrated from the countries listed in the official notice. For some reserved categories, candidates (or their forbears as the notice specifies) must satisfy the UP domicile requirement; **all vertical and horizontal reservation is limited to Uttar Pradesh natives**.

selectionProcess: **Written exam (300 marks, offline OMR) → shortlist in a multiple of the vacancies → Document verification + Physical Standard Test → PET (qualifying race) → Medical examination → Final merit list on written exam marks.** The merit list is prepared **category-wise from written exam marks only**; the PET and the physical standard test are pass-or-fail stages and carry no marks. Ties in marks are resolved in this order: candidates with a preferential qualification (NCC 'B' certificate, DOEACC/NIELIT 'O' level, or two years' regular army service) first, then the older candidate, then the candidate whose name comes earlier in English alphabetical order in the Class 10 certificate. There is no interview. Post allotment follows the merit-cum-preference order you filled in the application.
normalization: The written exam runs in many shifts across several days with different question papers, so the board applies its published **normalisation procedure** (notice dated 18 December 2023) to adjust scores across shifts before preparing the merit list. In practice: (1) never compare raw scores with candidates from other shifts; (2) attempt the paper you actually get, at its own pace; (3) a raw score a little below a cutoff you have heard about is not final — only the normalised score is compared. The OMR answer sheet is printed in three copies: the original goes to the board and you keep a copy.

faqs.q: What is the UP Police Constable written exam pattern?
faqs.a: One offline OMR paper: **150 objective questions, 2 marks each, 300 marks, 2 hours**, with four subjects — General Knowledge, General Hindi, Numerical and Mental Ability, and Mental Aptitude/IQ/Reasoning. There is no sectional timing. The official advertisement fixes the totals and the syllabus; the subject-wise question split (38 GK, 37 Hindi, 38 Numerical and Mental Ability, 37 Reasoning) follows the previous cycle's paper — confirm the final split from the board's exam-day notice.

faqs.q: Is there negative marking in UP Police Constable?
faqs.a: In the previous cycle's exam procedure, **0.5 marks were deducted for every wrong answer** (and for marking two options on one question), while each correct answer earned 2 marks. The 2025 advertisement sets 2 marks per correct answer but does not restate the penalty, so confirm it from the official exam instructions before guessing on the OMR sheet.

faqs.q: Does the PET carry marks? What decides the final merit?
faqs.a: No. The PET is **purely qualifying**: male candidates run 4.8 km in 25 minutes and female candidates run 2.4 km in 14 minutes. Fail the race and you are out, pass it and nothing is added. The **final merit list is built only from written exam marks**, category-wise.

As per the advertisement: **male minimum height 168 cm (ST 160 cm), chest 79 cm unexpanded and at least 84 cm expanded, with a minimum 5 cm expansion; female minimum height 152 cm (ST 147 cm) and minimum weight 40 kg**. Height and chest measured at this stage are final, whatever earlier certificates say.

faqs.q: What is the age limit for UP Police Constable?
faqs.a: For this cycle, as on **1 July 2025**: **18–22 years for male and 18–25 years for female** General/EWS candidates. SC, ST and OBC candidates of Uttar Pradesh get a maximum of 5 years' relaxation (male up to 27, female up to 30), and UP state government employees get 5 years. Ex-servicemen follow the notice's service-based table.

**₹500 for General, EWS and OBC candidates and ₹400 for SC/ST candidates**, as per the 2025 advertisement. The fee is paid online after submitting the OTR-based application; check the notice for the exact breakup of portal charges.

faqs.q: Can women apply for UP Police Constable?
faqs.a: Yes. Women can apply for **Constable (Civil Police), the Mahila Battalion Constable posts and Jail Warder (female)** — 2,282 vacancies are reserved in the Mahila Battalion alone, and women also compete within the Civil Police female quota. Armed Police, Special Security Force and Mounted Police posts are male-only in this notification.

faqs.q: What is the pay of a UP Police Constable?
faqs.a: All posts in this recruitment sit in **Pay Matrix Level 3: ₹21,700–69,100** (pay band 5200–20200 with Grade Pay 2000), plus the usual dearness allowance and allowances applicable to UP Police.

faqs.q: Do computer, NCC or army-service certificates help?
faqs.a: They give **no extra marks**, but they give **preference when candidates tie on equal marks**: a DOEACC/NIELIT 'O' level computer certificate, at least two years' service in the regular army, or an NCC 'B' certificate. A candidate holding more than one such qualification gets the benefit of only one.

faqs.q: What is the minimum qualifying marks in the written exam?
faqs.a: **30% for Unreserved candidates, 25% for OBC and 20% for SC/ST**, applied under the service rules named in the notice. Clearing the minimum alone is not enough — selection depends on your category-wise rank in the normalised written exam marks.

documents: Keep these ready for the application and for **document verification**: **Class 10 certificate** (date of birth proof), **Class 12 (Intermediate) marksheet**, **caste certificate in the prescribed UP format** (Prakoshtha-1 for SC/ST, Prakoshtha-2 for OBC, Prakoshtha-4 for EWS where applicable), **certified UP residence/domicile certificate** (needed for claiming any reservation), ex-servicemen or freedom-fighter-dependent certificate where applicable, **No Objection Certificate** for in-service candidates, **photo ID (Aadhaar preferred — the process uses Aadhaar-based authentication)**, a **real-time photograph** taken during the application, and your **scanned signature** (black ink on white paper, 50×20 mm). The board asks for certificates to be uploaded through **DigiLocker**, so keep your DigiLocker account active. Name and date of birth must match exactly across all documents — mismatches are the commonest cause of verification trouble.
